output.headline: Prosecutors set out case against man accused of killing British woman
output.standfirst: Prosecutors in Ocala, Florida, are setting out their case against Dwain Hall, accused of kidnapping and murdering Sonia Exelby, of Portsmouth, whose disappearance sparked an international search. Hall denies the charges.
output.bodyHtml:
Prosecutors in Ocala, Florida, have been setting out an extraordinary criminal case against Dwain C Hall, an auto repair and tow truck driver accused of kidnapping and murdering Sonia Exelby, of Portsmouth, England.

Hall has pleaded not guilty to the charges, which allege that he lured Exelby to the US before killing her in October last year and burying her body in a shallow grave in Marion Oaks.

Exelby’s disappearance from her home sparked an international investigation. After Hall’s arrest in November 2025, investigators said Exelby had travelled to Florida after posting online about wanting someone to end her life, and prosecutors this week described how she suffered from mental illness.

Hall’s arrest affidavit said Exelby had previously expressed suicidal thoughts, and investigators alleged that Hall knew about her struggles and used that vulnerability to bring her to Florida, the Ocala Starbanner reported.

Authorities have said Exelby boarded a flight to the US seemingly with an intention “to be possibly sexually abused, tortured, and murdered by unknown individuals living in the United States”.

After Exelby travelled to the US in October 2025, authorities say Hall picked her up from Gainesville airport in central Florida and drove her to an Airbnb rental, where investigators later found evidence they say connected him to her disappearance and death, including transactions on her bank cards and a video of Exelby on Hall’s cellphone.

In a text message from Exelby’s phone to a friend, she said she felt scared and trapped, according to the arrest affidavit. “I’m sorry, he keeps taking my phone, he doesn’t trust me with it,” she wrote. “He made it clear there was no way out unless I shoot him.”

In opening statements this week, assistant state attorney Amy Berndt said Exelby’s parents struggled with mental illness and addiction and that their daughter had also struggled with mental illness and twice attempted suicide.

She had visited a website depicting graphic sexual abuse of women, where Hall was among several men who contacted her.

Berndt said in court that Exelby “was trying to find some substitute” to the self-harm. “Unfortunately, she found another outlet.” Berndt said Exelby was “trying to find someone who would kill her”.

“Unfortunately there was no shortage of depraved men willing to kill Sonia in the most torturous and vile ways possible,” Berndt added.

After she disappeared from her home, a former boyfriend, Stevie Hunt, contacted the authorities, the court heard.

In court, Hunt described Exelby as a kind, beautiful and loving woman, while her sister talked about their difficult childhood. Hunt told the court that Exelby experienced mood swings that sometimes lasted for days and had been in therapy for more than a decade.

Hall has denied killing Exelby but acknowledged in a police interview that he had been in contact with her and that the two had been intimate. Evidence linking Hall to Exelby’s death includes a shovel with Exelby’s blood on it, cellphone data, and a knife recovered from a friend of the defendant.

Prosecutors have said jurors will be shown photographs and surveillance video of Hall making purchases including rope, a shovel, deodorant and other items at a local Walmart store.

Hall’s defense attorney Junior Barrett said in opening statements that his client was not a murderer and asked jurors to carefully consider the facts, witness testimony and circumstances of the case.

“We believe that when you listen to all the facts and evidence in this case, you will arrive at the decision that Dwain Hall did not murder,” Barrett said.

The case continues.
